title: The Road to Reims
description: June-July 1429. After the victory at Orleans, Joan of Arc must escort the Dauphin Charles through English-held territory to the cathedral at Reims for his coronation. English garrisons at Troyes and Chalons block the route and can be fought or persuaded to surrender. Victory requires the Dauphin reaching Reims cathedral alive; his death means defeat.

anachronisms_found: EL_CID placed as an English garrison commander: Rodrigo Diaz de Vivar died in 1099 and was a Castilian, not an Englishman - wrong century and wrong culture entirely

WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR placed as the second garrison commander: died 1087, some 340 years before the march to Reims; the engine offers Sir John Fastolf (an actual English commander of the 1429 campaign, shipped with the Joan of Arc campaign), so this was avoidable

English garrisons armed only with CROSSBOWMAN when the engine provides the Longbowman for exactly this English force; crossbows were more a Burgundian/continental garrison weapon than the signature English archery of 1429
Troyes and Chalons are labelled purely 'sworn to King Henry' and staffed as English; both were in practice Anglo-Burgundian towns, and no Burgundian presence is represented in text or roster

issues_found: Player 2 (the English/Burgundian garrisons of Troyes and Chalons) is commanded by EL_CID, an 11th-century Castilian who has no connection to the Hundred Years' War; the engine offers no 1429 English hero, but a renamed generic Champion/Knight would have been the correct substitution, so this is avoidable error.
WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR is the second garrison commander — right island, wrong century by 363 years; he is a Norman duke of 1066, not a Lancastrian captain of Henry VI's occupation.

Both players are set to civilization RANDOM, so architecture and unit skins for the French escort and the English garrison towns are undetermined; Franks/Britons were the obvious explicit assignments.

The garrisons are labelled purely 'English' in dialogue ('sworn to King Henry'); Troyes and Chalons were held by Anglo-Burgundian forces, and it was largely Burgundian allegiance that shifted, which the scenario never mentions.
The 'Forest Ambush' by 'English Scouts' with five patrolling groups is an invention — the march from Gien to Reims met no significant field engagement after Troyes capitulated.
Troyes 'Falls in Battle' by DESTROY_OBJECT on the garrison commander presents the town as stormable; historically the brief investment ended in negotiated surrender, not the killing of a commander.

Reims cathedral is represented only by a GAIA MONASTERY plus torches/flags — a thin stand-in for the coronation site that is the map's whole objective, given the engine's Wonder and cathedral-scale buildings were available.

Player 2 (the English garrisons of Troyes and Chalons) is led by EL_CID and WILLIAM_THE_CONQUEROR — an 11th-century Castilian and the Norman conqueror of 1066, neither English nor of the 1429 era. This was avoidable: the editor ships Hundred Years War heroes (e.g. Sir John Fastolf, Duke of Bedford-era generics) or a renamed generic knight/champion would have served.

Both players' civilizations are set to RANDOM, so architecture, unit skins and tech could render as Aztec, Japanese or Mongol — the French escort and English garrison have no assigned Frankish/Britons identity despite the engine offering both.
No Burgundian presence at all: Troyes and Chalons in July 1429 were Anglo-Burgundian towns, and the text attributes them solely to 'King Henry'.

Force scale is very thin for the march: the royal escort is 11 combatants plus Joan and the King, where the historical column was an army of roughly 12,000 that itself intimidated the towns into surrender.
The 'Forest Ambush' by English scouts on the Troyes-Reims road is invented; the sources record negotiation and submission of towns, not a woodland attack on the Dauphin's column.
A single MONASTERY stands in for Reims cathedral with no wonder or larger sacred structure, and the coronation site is marked only by a flag/area.
